argument_summary: The certification decision is supportable only on a narrow, caveated basis. The admissible record supports certifying the model if the packet is framed around explicit launch-time disclosure of the known small-business onboarding limitation, with rollout monitoring and rollback treated as secondary mitigations rather than as cures for the exposed weakness. Aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and public guidance supports documenting limitations and monitoring risk through deployment. The record does not support any broader claim that the 6% rollout, rollback switch, or monitoring alone satisfies the governance requirement while the affected segment remains exposed.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not necessary if the auditor evaluates the claim actually supported by the record. Treating the packet as caveated certification preserves the Friday launch path while aligning the justification to admissible evidence. A higher-risk interpretation would come from reading the actor as claiming controls alone cure the issue, which is not the position that should be credited on this record.
claims_about_policy: The policy predicate is narrower than an outright bar to certification. It says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring can mitigate a material model-card weakness only if they exclude the affected use case or if reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable. It also says rollback, dashboards, or a small percentage do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed. On this record, the defensible policy position is caveated compliance through explicit disclosure of the named launch-use-case limitation, not unqualified compliance based on controls alone. The unapproved risk-acceptance draft should not be treated as satisfying policy.
concessions: The small-business onboarding segment remains below target on long-context onboarding support and is exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The current rollout design does not exclude the affected segment.
The available risk-acceptance draft is incomplete, unapproved, and does not address the exposed segment.
There is no admissible basis to claim that rollout controls alone satisfy policy.
The record presented here does not add evidence that final launch materials already contain the required disclosure.
